notes: Known wrong -> right Mathlib names for the pinned toolchain. When Lean reports one of the wrong names as an unknown identifier, the worker substitutes the right name and recompiles before asking a model to repair. To extend, add a row: `example` must fail with the wrong name (unknown identifier) and compile once the right name is substituted, at the pinned Lean and Mathlib; tests check every row. Add a row only if the right name takes the same arguments in the same order; a name that is merely deprecated still compiles and needs no row. No code change is needed.

entries.note: Mathlib names the triangle inequality `abs_add_le`; `abs_add` does not exist.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) : |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b| := abs_add a b

entries.note: The ordered-field `div_le_iff` was removed after its deprecation; the `₀` lemma has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (h : a ≤ b * c) : a / c ≤ b := (div_le_iff hc).mpr h

entries.note: The ordered-field `le_div_iff` was removed after its deprecation; the `₀` lemma has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (h : a * c ≤ b) : a ≤ b / c := (le_div_iff hc).mpr h

entries.note: The ordered-field `lt_div_iff` was removed after its deprecation; the `₀` lemma has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (h : a * c < b) : a < b / c := (lt_div_iff hc).mpr h

entries.note: The ordered-field `div_lt_iff` was removed after its deprecation; the `₀` lemma has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (h : a < b * c) : a / c < b := (div_lt_iff hc).mpr h

entries.note: The primed `div_le_iff'` was removed after its deprecation; `div_le_iff₀'` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (h : a ≤ c * b) : a / c ≤ b := (div_le_iff' hc).mpr h

entries.note: The primed `le_div_iff'` was removed after its deprecation; `le_div_iff₀'` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (h : c * a ≤ b) : a ≤ b / c := (le_div_iff' hc).mpr h

entries.note: The primed `lt_div_iff'` was removed after its deprecation; `lt_div_iff₀'` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (h : c * a < b) : a < b / c := (lt_div_iff' hc).mpr h

entries.note: The primed `div_lt_iff'` was removed after its deprecation; `div_lt_iff₀'` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (h : a < c * b) : a / c < b := (div_lt_iff' hc).mpr h

entries.note: `div_le_div_iff` was removed after its deprecation; `div_le_div_iff₀` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b c d : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (hd : 0 < d) (h : a * d ≤ b * c) : a / c ≤ b / d := (div_le_div_iff hc hd).mpr h

entries.note: `div_le_div_right` was removed after its deprecation; the replacement takes the same positivity hypothesis.
entries.example: example (a b c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (h : a ≤ b) : a / c ≤ b / c := (div_le_div_right hc).mpr h

entries.note: `div_lt_div_right` was removed after its deprecation; the replacement takes the same positivity hypothesis.
entries.example: example (a b c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (h : a < b) : a / c < b / c := (div_lt_div_right hc).mpr h

entries.note: `div_le_div_left` was removed after its deprecation; the replacement takes the same three positivity hypotheses.
entries.example: example (a b c : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c) (h : c ≤ b) : a / b ≤ a / c := (div_le_div_left ha hb hc).mpr h

entries.note: `div_lt_div_left` was removed after its deprecation; the replacement takes the same three positivity hypotheses.
entries.example: example (a b c : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c) (h : c < b) : a / b < a / c := (div_lt_div_left ha hb hc).mpr h

entries.note: `inv_le_inv` was removed after its deprecation; `inv_le_inv₀` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : b ≤ a) : a⁻¹ ≤ b⁻¹ := (inv_le_inv ha hb).mpr h

entries.note: `inv_lt_inv` was removed after its deprecation; `inv_lt_inv₀` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : b < a) : a⁻¹ < b⁻¹ := (inv_lt_inv ha hb).mpr h

entries.note: There is no `one_div_le_one_div_iff`; the iff is `one_div_le_one_div` with the same two positivity hypotheses.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : b ≤ a) : 1 / a ≤ 1 / b := (one_div_le_one_div_iff ha hb).mpr h

entries.note: There is no `one_div_lt_one_div_iff`; the iff is `one_div_lt_one_div` with the same two positivity hypotheses.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : b < a) : 1 / a < 1 / b := (one_div_lt_one_div_iff ha hb).mpr h

entries.note: `pow_le_pow_left` was removed after its deprecation; `pow_le_pow_left₀` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : a ≤ b) : a ^ 3 ≤ b ^ 3 := pow_le_pow_left ha hab 3

entries.note: The Lean 3 name `pow_le_pow_of_le_left` is gone; `pow_le_pow_left₀` takes the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : a ≤ b) : a ^ 3 ≤ b ^ 3 := pow_le_pow_of_le_left ha hab 3

entries.note: `pow_lt_pow_left` was removed after its deprecation; `pow_lt_pow_left₀` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : a < b) : a ^ 3 < b ^ 3 := pow_lt_pow_left hab ha (by norm_num)

entries.note: `pow_le_pow_right` was removed after its deprecation; `pow_le_pow_right₀` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a : ℝ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (h : 2 ≤ 5) : a ^ 2 ≤ a ^ 5 := pow_le_pow_right ha h

entries.note: `pow_lt_pow_right` was removed after its deprecation; `pow_lt_pow_right₀` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a : ℝ) (ha : 1 < a) (h : 2 < 5) : a ^ 2 < a ^ 5 := pow_lt_pow_right ha h

entries.note: The Lean 3 name `pow_lt_pow` is gone; `pow_lt_pow_right₀` takes the same two hypotheses.
entries.example: example (a : ℝ) (ha : 1 < a) (h : 2 < 5) : a ^ 2 < a ^ 5 := pow_lt_pow ha h

entries.note: `pow_lt_pow_iff_left` was removed after its deprecation; `pow_lt_pow_iff_left₀` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) : a ^ 2 < b ^ 2 ↔ a < b := pow_lt_pow_iff_left ha hb (by norm_num)

entries.note: `pow_lt_pow_iff_right` was removed after its deprecation; `pow_lt_pow_iff_right₀` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a : ℝ) (ha : 1 < a) : a ^ 2 < a ^ 5 ↔ 2 < 5 := pow_lt_pow_iff_right ha

entries.note: `one_lt_pow` was removed after its deprecation; `one_lt_pow₀` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a : ℝ) (ha : 1 < a) : 1 < a ^ 3 := one_lt_pow ha (by norm_num)

entries.note: `lt_of_pow_lt_pow_left` was removed after its deprecation; `lt_of_pow_lt_pow_left₀` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (h : a ^ 2 < b ^ 2) : a < b := lt_of_pow_lt_pow_left 2 hb h

entries.note: `le_of_pow_le_pow_left` was removed after its deprecation; `le_of_pow_le_pow_left₀` has the same arguments.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (h : a ^ 2 ≤ b ^ 2) : a ≤ b := le_of_pow_le_pow_left (by norm_num) hb h

entries.note: The Lean 3 name `sub_eq_zero_iff_eq` is gone; `sub_eq_zero` states the same iff.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (h : a - b = 0) : a = b := sub_eq_zero_iff_eq.mp h

entries.note: There is no `mul_eq_zero_iff`; `mul_eq_zero` states the same iff.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (h : a * b = 0) : a = 0 ∨ b = 0 := mul_eq_zero_iff.mp h

entries.note: The Lean 3 name `add_right_neg` was removed; `add_neg_cancel` states the same equation.
entries.example: example (a : ℝ) : a + -a = 0 := add_right_neg a

entries.note: The Lean 3 name `add_left_neg` was removed; `neg_add_cancel` states the same equation.
entries.example: example (a : ℝ) : -a + a = 0 := add_left_neg a

entries.note: The Lean 3 name `add_sub_cancel'` was removed; `add_sub_cancel_left` states `a + b - a = b`.
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) : a + b - a = b := add_sub_cancel' a b

entries.note: `not_lt_of_le` was removed; `not_lt_of_ge` has the same shape (a ≤ b gives ¬ b < a).
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (h : a ≤ b) : ¬ b < a := not_lt_of_le h

entries.note: `not_le_of_lt` was removed; `not_le_of_gt` has the same shape (a < b gives ¬ b ≤ a).
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (h : a < b) : ¬ b ≤ a := not_le_of_lt h

entries.note: `le_of_not_lt` was removed; `le_of_not_gt` has the same shape (¬ b < a gives a ≤ b).
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (h : ¬ b < a) : a ≤ b := le_of_not_lt h

entries.note: `lt_of_not_le` was removed; `lt_of_not_ge` has the same shape (¬ b ≤ a gives a < b).
entries.example: example (a b : ℝ) (h : ¬ b ≤ a) : a < b := lt_of_not_le h

entries.note: Without `open Real` the bare name is unknown; the real-number lemma is `Real.sq_sqrt`.
entries.example: example (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x) : Real.sqrt x ^ 2 = x := sq_sqrt hx

entries.note: Without `open Real` the bare name is unknown; the real-number lemma is `Real.sqrt_sq`.
entries.example: example (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x) : Real.sqrt (x ^ 2) = x := sqrt_sq hx

entries.note: Without `open Filter` the bare name is unknown; the lemma is `Filter.tendsto_pow_atTop`.
entries.example: example : Filter.Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => x ^ 2) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop := tendsto_pow_atTop (by norm_num)
